column1: # Danish (da) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#            @plural              `source` is "one|other" (English forms); the translation lists the
#                                 language's forms separated by "|" (see `plural` in i18n.rs)
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Based on the community Danish catalog in #7267, completed for the current UI: its rows were
# checked and corrected, the strings added since were translated, and one term is used per concept
# across the UI (lag, markering, maske, gradient, blød kant, transformér/transformering, vridning,
# gitter, hjælpelinje, tavle, lærred, udklipningsmaske, arbejdsområde, pensel, blandingstilstand,
# justering, kanal, sti, historik, forudindstilling, øjebliksbillede, form, kontur, nål …).
# Clean-room: written from the plain meaning of the English labels using ordinary Danish computing
# vocabulary; no proprietary localisation resource, string table or product UI was consulted or
# copied. Labels use sentence case, commands are imperatives and the user is addressed as "du".
# Product, format and technology names (PhotoCraft, ArtCraft, OpenType, CMYK, Lab …) and key caps
# keep their spelling; the trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept. Plural rule: one|other
# (n != 1 -> other). Native-speaker review of the remaining specialist terms is welcome.
